params.prompt:
1950s theatrical cartoon slapstick, hand-drawn colored-pencil pencil-test animation on cream paper, held on twos with visible line boil. Fixed camera, locked tripod, one continuous shot.

The young man in the office chair, facing us, sits up, his brows set and his eyes sharp, and lifts his right hand off the armrest. He points sharply up and away over his right shoulder towards the far left of the frame — his head and eyes turn to follow his own finger, his brows lift, and his lips move as he mouths a short, clear instruction, then he gives one firm nod. He swings the point down and to the left, low and close towards the camera, his face turning with it, lips moving on another short instruction, a firm nod. He swings the point straight out at the camera, past us, eyes right down the lens, lips moving, a nod. He swings it up and away over his left shoulder towards the far right of the frame, his head turning after it, lips moving on the last instruction, a nod. Then he opens both hands palms up in a small "go on" gesture, his face breaking into a wide grin, drops his hands back onto the armrests, and settles, grinning, with one last slow nod.

His eyes stay open in every frame and go where his finger goes. His mouth moves whenever he is giving an instruction and closes into a smile when he settles. His expression is determined and bright: brows set, eyes sharp, the face alive and changing with every point. His short blonde hair, his stubble and his navy T-shirt are the same in every frame. He stays seated in the same chair on the same spot on the floor in every frame, and the chair stays turned towards us in every frame. The desk, the three monitors, the cork board, the whiteboard, the printer bench, the shelf of binders, the lamp, the mug, the bell and the striped cannon stay the same drawings in every frame.

Squash and stretch on every accent, smear frames through the fast arcs, snappy timing, elastic overshoot, comic energy.
